form.label: CVE encyclopaedia
form.description: Look up any vulnerability the feed carries, and see where it sits in this fleet. Entirely offline.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_cvedetail_lookup | stats count AS rk_rows

div.b: This bundle carries no CVE Program catalogue, so the descriptions and product names on this page are missing rather than unknown.
div.span: Findings come from OSV and the distribution advisories, which name a package and a version but rarely describe the vulnerability. The description, the product names and the free text search on this page come from the CVE Program catalogue instead, and that is opt in when the feed is built because it is the largest source by far. A CVE with a finding but no entry here is one this bundle cannot describe, not one nobody has described. Rebuild the feed with --cve-list and import it to fill this in. Everything else on this page, the matching, the severity, the KEV status and the affected ranges, works without it.

div.b: Nothing on this page is fetched from the internet.
div.span: It is read from the bundle you imported, so it says what that bundle knew when it was built and nothing more. A CVE that returns nothing is one the feed has never carried, which is not the same as one that is harmless. Coverage lists which sources the bundle actually holds.

search.query: | `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | stats max(cvss_score) AS rk_max, count AS rk_n | eval v = if(isnull(rk_max), "not scored", tostring(round(rk_max,1))) | where rk_n > 0 | fields v
| `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | stats max(epss) AS rk_max, count AS rk_n | eval v = if(isnull(rk_max), "unscored", tostring(round(rk_max*100,1)) . "%") | where rk_n > 0 | fields v

| `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | stats count AS rk_n, count(eval(kev_added != "")) AS rk_kev | eval v = case(rk_n == 1 AND rk_kev == 1, "YES", rk_n == 1, "not listed", rk_kev == 0, "none of " . rk_n, 1=1, rk_kev . " of " . rk_n) | where rk_n > 0 | fields v
| inputlookup riskability_findings_state_lookup where cve_id="$cve_tok$" AND status="open" | stats dc(hostname) AS v | where "$cve_tok$" != ""

single.option: hosts reporting it open; zero is not "unaffected"

div.span: The four figures above summarise whatever the inputs matched, and everything below lists it. Name one CVE and they describe that one; use a wildcard such as CVE-2023-486* and they describe the set, which is why they read "worst" and "highest" rather than giving a single vulnerability's score. Empty means nothing was matched, not that anything was found to be harmless.

panel.title: What the feed says these are

search.query: | `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | lookup riskability_cvedetail_lookup cve_id OUTPUT products AS rk_products, description AS rk_desc, assigner AS rk_assigner, published AS rk_pub | eval Product = case(coalesce(rk_products,"") != "", replace(rk_products, " ", ", "), kev_name != "", kev_name, 1=1, "not named by the feed") | eval Description = case(coalesce(rk_desc,"") != "", rk_desc, kev_description != "", kev_description, best_title != "", best_title, 1=1, "No advisory in this bundle carries a description for this CVE.") | eval Severity = coalesce(severity, ""), CVSS = coalesce(cvss_score, "") | eval "EPSS %" = if(isnotnull(epss), round(epss*100, 1), null()) | eval KEV = if(kev_added != "", "yes", "") | eval Published = trim(coalesce(rk_assigner,"") . " " . coalesce(rk_pub, published)) | table cve_id, Product, Description, Severity, CVSS, "EPSS %", KEV, Published | rename cve_id AS CVE | sort 200 - CVSS

viz.option: Name a CVE above, pick a row from the search results further down, or click any CVE id anywhere else in this app. Wildcards work: "CVE-2023-486*" lists every one that matches, one row each.

div.span: One row per vulnerability, never merged. The description falls back in turn: the CVE Program's own record, then CISA's wording if it is known exploited, then the longest advisory text in the bundle. That last fallback matters, because distribution advisories often carry no prose at all, and taking the longest of the several describing one CVE recovers a description for 640,830 of the 641,374 the feed knows about. The product name has no such fallback: only the CVE Program and CISA ever state one.

panel.title: What CISA says, and by when

search.query: | `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | where kev_added != "" | eval "Added" = kev_added | eval "Remediate by" = if(kev_due != "", kev_due, "no date given") | eval "Ransomware" = if(kev_ransomware != "", kev_ransomware, "not stated") | eval "CISA calls it" = if(kev_title != "", kev_title, "") | eval "What CISA requires" = if(kev_action != "", kev_action, "The entry in this bundle carries no required action. Bundles built before this app kept those fields hold only the dates.") | table cve_id, "CISA calls it", Added, "Remediate by", Ransomware, "What CISA requires" | rename cve_id AS CVE | sort 200 "Remediate by"

viz.option: Not in the CISA KEV catalogue, or no CVE is selected. Absence from the catalogue is not evidence that a vulnerability is unexploited; it means CISA has not observed and published exploitation of it.

div.span: The catalogue is the one source here that reports observation rather than modelling: an entry means exploitation was seen in the wild, not predicted. Remediate by is CISA's deadline for US federal agencies. It carries no legal weight elsewhere, and is still the most defensible date to argue a change window against.

panel.title: What an attacker needs, from the CVSS vector

search.query: | `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | `riskability_cvss_english` | table cve_id, Vector, Reach, Complexity, Privileges, "User interaction", Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability | rename cve_id AS CVE | sort 200 CVE

viz.option: No CVSS vector for this CVE in the feed.

div.span: The vector spelled out, nothing more. It describes the vulnerability as published, not this fleet. Whether your copy answers a network address is a different question, and the Exposure page answers it.

panel.title: Weakness class, and the techniques mapped to it

search.query: | `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | fields cve_id, cwes | mvexpand cwes | rename cwes AS cwe | where cwe != "" | lookup riskability_attack_lookup cwe OUTPUT technique, technique_name, tactics, via_capec | eval Technique = if(isnull(technique), "no ATT&CK mapping in this bundle", technique . " " . technique_name) | eval Tactics = mvjoin(tactics, ", ") | stats values(Technique) AS Technique, values(Tactics) AS Tactics BY cve_id, cwe | rename cve_id AS CVE, cwe AS CWE | sort 300 CVE, CWE

viz.option: No weakness class recorded for this CVE. About a third of advisories carry no CWE, and the technique mapping needs the MITRE source in the bundle.

panel.title: Find a vulnerability by product or phrase

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_cvedetail_lookup | search products="*$q_tok$*" OR description="*$q_tok$*" OR cve_id="*$q_tok$*" | head 200 | eval Product = mvindex(split(products, " "), 0) | lookup riskability_advisories_lookup cve_id OUTPUT severity, cvss_score, epss, kev_added | eval Severity = coalesce(severity, ""), CVSS = coalesce(cvss_score, ""), "EPSS %" = if(isnotnull(epss), round(epss*100, 1), null()), KEV = if(coalesce(kev_added, "")!="", "yes", "") | table cve_id, Product, Severity, CVSS, "EPSS %", KEV | rename cve_id AS CVE | sort 200 - CVSS

viz.option: Type a product, a vendor or a phrase in the search box at the top. "openssl", "Red Hat", "buffer overflow". This searches the CVE Program product names and description text, so it finds vulnerabilities by what they are rather than by what your distribution happened to call the package. It needs a bundle built with the CVE Program source; without one, use the CVE box instead.

div.span: Click any row to load it above. This searches the feed, not this fleet, which is the point: an encyclopaedia has to be able to tell you about something you do not run. Capped at 200, worst CVSS first.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_findings_state_lookup where cve_id="$cve_tok$" | eval rk_key = if(match(coalesce(scope_id, ""), "^container:"), "container:" . substr(replace(scope_id, "^container:", ""), 1, 12), package) | lookup riskability_reach_lookup hostname, rk_key OUTPUT reach_class | eval Reach = coalesce(reach_class, "not assessed") | eval Accepted = if(accepted="1", "yes", "") | eval path = replace(path, "\\\\\\\\", "\\\\") | table cve_id, hostname, package, last_version, fixed_version, path, scope, confidence, Reach, status, Accepted | rename cve_id AS CVE, hostname AS Host, package AS Package, last_version AS Installed, fixed_version AS "Fixed in", path AS "Found at", scope AS Scope, confidence AS Confidence, status AS Status | sort 500 CVE, Host, Package

viz.option: Nothing in this fleet matches this CVE. That means no host reports an affected package at an affected version. It does not mean immunity: Coverage lists what the feed cannot assess at all.

panel.title: Which versions fix what, across distributions

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_ranges_lookup where cve_id="$cve_tok$" | where fixed != "" | eval rk_pkg = replace(ecosystem . " " . package, "[|]", "_") | eval rk_fix = replace(package . " " . fixed . if(distro="", "", " (" . distro . ")"), "[|]", "_") | eval rk_hops = mvappend(cve_id . "|cve|" . rk_pkg . "|pkg", rk_pkg . "|pkg|" . rk_fix . "|fix") | mvexpand rk_hops | eval rk_p = split(rk_hops, "|") | eval source = mvindex(rk_p, 0), source_kind = mvindex(rk_p, 1), target = mvindex(rk_p, 2), target_kind = mvindex(rk_p, 3) | stats count AS cves BY source, source_kind, target, target_kind | sort 240 - cves | fields source, source_kind, target, target_kind, cves

viz.option: No fixed version for this CVE in the bundle. That is common and is not an error: an advisory that names no fix has none published, so there is no upgrade to point at. Check the affected ranges below for whether a later version is merely "last affected".

div.span: Read left to right: the vulnerability, the package each ecosystem calls it, and the version that fixes it there. One CVE fans out across every packaging of it, which is why a single vulnerability can need a dozen separate upgrades; name several and the columns consolidate rather than becoming unreadable. These are the feed's fix versions, not a patch plan for this fleet. Nothing here knows which of these you run or at what version. Matching hosts in this fleet above is the panel that does. Version nodes carry their package and distribution, because two packages fixing at "1.2.3" are not one node and merging them would draw a route that does not exist. Crowded columns collapse into a single node rather than becoming unreadable.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_ranges_lookup where cve_id="$cve_tok$" | eval Introduced = if(introduced="", "any earlier version", introduced) | eval Fixed = case(fixed != "", fixed, last_affected != "", "no fix; last affected " . last_affected, 1=1, "no fix published") | eval Distribution = trim(distro . " " . distro_release) | stats values(Fixed) AS Fixed, values(Introduced) AS Introduced BY cve_id, ecosystem, package, Distribution | rename cve_id AS CVE, ecosystem AS Ecosystem, package AS Package | sort 500 CVE, Ecosystem, Package, Distribution

viz.option: No affected ranges for this CVE in the bundle.

div.span: One CVE usually has several advisories: the upstream one, and one per distribution that shipped a fix. They disagree about version numbers on purpose, because each describes its own packaging.
